what_was_owed: a public benchmark number. Every result in rounds 34-72 was measured on pages authored inside this repo, which is a closed loop and cannot be evidence for anything general.

benchmark.name: MiniWob++ (Farama Foundation, pip miniwob 1.1.0, git clone 2026-08)
benchmark.selection_by_author: none -- the list is the contents of the html directory
benchmark.goal_source: the live page's #query element at run time
benchmark.scoring: WOB_REWARD_GLOBAL > 0, read AFTER the episode, never in scope when acting
benchmark.clock: MiniWob++ decays reward by time inside each episode, so these scores are not comparable to an untimed benchmark

published_comparison.verdict: 7x to 8x below the best published systems. This is not competitive and must not be presented as such.

the_finding_that_matters_more_than_the_s.addressable: 113/130 tasks exposed named or interactive structure = 86.9% (measured, census_130_v1.json)
the_finding_that_matters_more_than_the_s.used_by_the_policy: the parser bucketed 87/130 goals as 'unknown' and attempted nothing
the_finding_that_matters_more_than_the_s.conclusion: the ladder solved WHERE things are. It solved nothing about WHAT the instruction means. The binding constraint was always the parser, and 86.9% addressability means the ceiling was never the page.

the_three_harness_bugs_that_produced_thr: ax_nodes returns a box, not x/y -- every click raised KeyError and the per-task except swallowed it: reported 0/25
Input.dispatchKeyEvent was not on the score channel allowlist -- every typing task failed silently: reported 2/25 then 6/25
the first 0/25 was 100% instrument error. A benchmark score is worth exactly the credibility of the harness, and mine was wrong three times before it was right.
honest_reading_rules: allowed: the goal sentence from the live page (it is the user's instruction)
allowed: roles, accessible names, geometry of the current screen
banned: task HTML/JS source to find answers
banned: reading the reward before or during an action
no per-task code, no task-name special-casing, no model
what_this_proves: a zero-model, zero-parameter agent acts correctly on published tasks it has never seen
structure addressing is not specific to pages authored here
what_this_does_not_prove: competitiveness -- it is 7x worse than GPT-4 on the same suite
generality -- the goal parser covers a handful of shapes
next: write the goal parser as a proper semantic layer, not a regex ladder
measure how far the parser alone moves the number at zero model calls
then re-measure with the model in the decision seat, rung 3, and report the cost delta
